Thanks for the signal and the artifacts — reproduced locally against staging using their curl. Preliminary root cause: a bug in our JS client SDK (sdk-js v2.1.5) that serializes headers using LF-only ("\n") instead of CRLF ("\r\n") in a small codepath that handles streamed requests. Two consequences we observed:

1) Our streaming parser assumes CRLF header termination to split headers from the body; LF-only sequences are being treated as part of the first data chunk in some runtimes, leading the parser to mis-detect framing.
2) In a minority of cases the client also sends duplicate pseudo-headers (x-client-proto/x-stream-binary) in a single header block; our runtime's header de-dup logic triggers an assert and causes a short-circuit close (TCP FIN) instead of an app-level error response.

Repro snippet (staging):
-- observed raw header block --
POST /v1/streams/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
x-client-proto: 1.0
x-client-proto: 1.0

<binary chunk>
-- end --

Stack trace (trimmed):
runtime/src/stream_parser.cc:line 412: parse_headers() -> invalid_header_termination
runtime/src/connection.cc:line 278: on_data() -> assert(header_unique)

Immediate mitigations we can deploy:
- Hotfix 1 (fast): tolerate LF-only header terminations in the staging->prod parser (server-side patch). Canary + rollback safe.
- Hotfix 2 (parallel): add header normalization proxy rule at our ingress (Nginx) to replace LF-only with CRLF and coalesce duplicate pseudo-headers.
- Medium term: release sdk-js v2.1.6 that normalizes outgoing header serialization and adds a test for header framing.

I'll open INC-1724 and a PR for a parser-tolerance patch. Recommend we push server-side tolerance to canary within 4 hours, and the Nginx rule within 8 hours.

— Rishi
